rationale: User: '2D is slop - i need direct biological shown in 3D'. AF2/Boltz GPU-gated (all 3 folds timed out after 16h). Pivoted to REAL deposited experimental crystal structures from RCSB (ground-truth 3D, drugs/DNA already bound, no GPU). Renders are illustrative views of deposited structures; experimental evidence is STRONGER than model confidence. Labeled honestly as experimental with PDB ID + resolution + method. RUO.

engine.compose: analysis/pdb3d_compose.py (render: light structure-forward chrome + global-palette no-dither GIF)
key_fixes: cmd.reinitialize() at start of every render -> prevents PyMOL state leakage between structures in a batch (leaked cartoon_transparency/orient had blanked the DNA render)
NO on-atom cmd.label (collide/clip in orbit) -> all text added by matplotlib compositor at fixed positions
single stable camera per render (orient+zoom once, no re-zoom mid-orbit) -> no edge clipping
drug/mutation: single chain isolated from multi-copy AU -> one prominent protein+drug, not tiny duplicates
drug/mutation: semi-transparent cartoon -> buried drug/residue stays visible from all angles
GIF: global 64-color palette + dither=NONE + frame_step + 0.82 scale -> 25MB -> ~5MB, media-check-verified quality

animations.biology: KRAS G12C  —  sotorasib locked in the mutant pocket
animations.verified: residue 12 = CYS (G12C confirmed); ligand MOV = sotorasib/AMG510 (41 atoms) + GDP + Mg
animations.on_frame_caption: Sotorasib (AMG 510) binds covalently to the mutant Cys12, trapping KRAS inactive — the drug–target event in a real 1.65 Å crystal structure. Evo2 scores G12C as sequence-tolerated (Δll −0.148): the oncogenic switch looks normal to a language model but is a validated drug target here.

manuscript_number_provenance.Evo2 dll G12C = -0.148: M12 Evo2 panel (tolerated; oncogenic switch looks normal to LM)

animations.biology: PARP1  —  olaparib in the NAD⁺ catalytic site
animations.verified: ligand 09L = olaparib; 2 copies in AU, chain A rendered
animations.on_frame_caption: Olaparib occupies the NAD⁺ pocket of the PARP1 catalytic domain — a real drug-binding event shown structurally. NOTE: in Manuscript 00 the MBD4-LOF → PARP-therapy axis is FALSIFIED (PARP1 not upregulated, p=0.605); this frame shows only how the PARP inhibitor engages the enzyme, not an MBD4 therapy claim.

manuscript_number_provenance.p=0.605: M00 PARP1 NOT upregulated in MBD4-LOF (Mann-Whitney, n=19 LOF vs 1498 WT, DepMap 24Q2). Frame explicitly states MBD4->PARP axis is FALSIFIED; render shows only drug-enzyme engagement.

animations.biology: BACE1  —  β-secretase apex driver, druggable pocket
animations.verified: ligand 32D = AZD3839 clinical BACE1 inhibitor; catalytic Asp32 present
animations.on_frame_caption: BACE1 is the apex brain-metastasis driver in Manuscript 12 (CRISPRa LFC +7.28; 156-fold up in brain mets; ZERO somatic mutations). Here a clinical β-secretase inhibitor (AZD3839) sits between the catalytic aspartates — an Alzheimer's-repurposable pocket, invisible to mutation-centric panels.

animations.biology: EGFR L858R  —  activating mutation + covalent inhibitor
animations.verified: residue 858 = ARG (L858R confirmed); ligand DJK covalent quinazoline inhibitor
animations.on_frame_caption: The L858R activating mutation sits in the EGFR kinase activation loop; a covalent quinazoline inhibitor occupies the ATP pocket. Evo2 scores L858R as sequence-tolerated (Δll +0.088) — an activating oncogenic change that looks normal to a language model, underscoring why structure + function, not sequence alone, defines driver impact.

animations.biology: PIK3CA H1047R  —  hotspot at the kinase C-terminus
animations.verified: residue 1047 = ARG (H1047R confirmed) - true mutant structure (4JPS was WT, rejected)
animations.on_frame_caption: H1047R is a recurrent PI3Kα activating hotspot in the kinase domain C-terminal tail, shown here in the real mutant crystal structure. Evo2 flags H1047R as disruptive (Δll −0.615), consistent with a structurally consequential change to the catalytic machinery.

animations.biology: p53  —  DNA-binding domain gripping its response element
animations.verified: 3 p53 monomers (chains A/B/C) + DNA duplex (chains E/F, 855 nucleic atoms); Arg248 & Arg273 DNA-contact arginines present; Zn structural ion; chain A rendered on DNA
animations.on_frame_caption: The p53 core domain reads DNA through direct contacts: Arg248 inserts into the minor groove and Arg273 contacts the phosphate backbone. Hotspot mutations at these arginines (e.g. R248W, R273H) abolish DNA binding — the structural basis of p53 loss-of-function. Evo2 scores the DNA-contact R248W as tolerated (Δll +0.099): sequence conservation alone misses contact-residue drivers.
